response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT CENTROMEA AS status, AVG(HGB) AS avg_hgb, AVG(`T-BIL` / CRE) AS avg_ratio FROM Laboratory WHERE Date > '1985-04-22' AND Date < '1994-03-14' GROUP BY CENTROMEA), o AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS overall_mean FROM g) SELECT g.status, g.avg_hgb, g.avg_ratio, g.avg_ratio / o.overall_mean AS ratio_to_overall_mean FROM g CROSS JOIN o WHERE o.overall_mean IS NOT NULL;

assumptions.assumption: Laboratory.Date is stored as ISO text (YYYY-MM-DD), so the string comparisons against '1985-04-22' and '1994-03-14' order dates correctly. The documentation says YYMMDD, which would make these comparisons wrong.

Each row's ratio is T-BIL / CRE, with NULL when either value is missing or CRE is zero (SQLite returns NULL for division by zero). Each group's average ratio is the mean of these per-row ratios, not the ratio of averages.
A NULL CENTROMEA forms its own group through GROUP BY, and it is returned with a NULL status. Empty-string statuses are not treated as missing.
The overall mean is the unweighted AVG of the group-level average ratios, skipping any group whose average ratio is NULL. If that overall mean is NULL, no rows are returned.
